title: Ex-Colorado State AD, former players raise alarm over Jim Mora and staff conduct
summary: Former Colorado State players have sent a letter to the university's governing board to address concerns about Jim Mora and his coaching staff.
content: Things appear to continue to get messier for Jim Mora at Colorado State. According to The Coloradan — part of the USA TODAY Network — nearly two dozen former Colorado State players are asking the university’s governing board to address concerns in what they describe as "inappropriate behaviors" from Mora and his staff and "the lack of response by athletic department leadership." Mora is in his first season at Colorado State after being hired from UConn last offseason. Week 13 bold predictions: Rivalry weekend could wreck some playoff dreams The Colorado State players who wrote and sent the letter to the Colorado State University System Board of Governors on Nov. 25 include former Rams quarterback and athletic director Jack Graham, former defensive back Erik Olson and former linebacker Nate Kvamme. The letter does not specifically ask the Colorado State University System Board of Governors to fire Mora or Colorado State athletic director John Weber, but brings forth their worry about the "welfare of the student athletes" in the program. "As former CSU football players, we want to convey a sense of urgency and resolve to support the University in rebuilding the integrity, culture and reputation of the Athletic Department and our football program," the letter reads. "Our experiences at CSU delivered great lessons and guidance for our adult lives. "We learned to compete and win. We had support to study and succeed in our academic careers. We were given the opportunity to be part of teams that represented commitment, hard work, integrity, respect and pride. We left CSU as better people." Graham additionally brought up several "red flag" incidents that he believes are egregious enough for Colorado State to fire Mora "for cause" under the terms of the five-year contract they signed him to last December. These "red flags" include: the program’s entire equipment room staff reportedly quitting at the beginning of the season or late spring due to "abusive behavior toward them by Jim Mora," damage allegedly done to the visitors’ locker room following a loss at Texas State on Oct. 25, not believing Mora's side of the story on the firing of former Rams defensive coordinator Tyson Summers in the middle of a game against Oregon State on Oct. 3 and a physical altercation between strength and conditioning coach Shelton Bynum and offensive lineman Toriyan Johnson amongst others. REQYIRED READING: Pac-12 flex week is set: Who will Boise State, others play? "Is the University providing the culture, leadership, support and resources these athletes need to be good human beings, strong competitors and lifelong proud alumnae of CSU?," the letter reads. "... We believe not; rather, they are seeing the antithesis of these critical values." Under Mora this season, the Rams have the No.4 scoring offense in the Pac-12 at 33.7 points per game, but one of the worst defenses in the conference and country. The Rams rank dead last in the Pac-12 in both scoring defense at 47.7 points per game and total defense at 548.1 total yards allowed per game. The Rams have won just once in their last nine games and have lost each of their last four games. In their four-game losing skid, Colorado State has been outscored by opponents 217-101. Colorado State ends its regular season at 6 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 28 against No. 21 Boise State . title: Ohio State football Michigan hype video: 'FIGHT LIKE HELL'
summary: Ohio State dropped its Michigan-week trailer Thursday. Fire, legends, and one message: FIGHT LIKE HELL. The Game kicks off Saturday at noon on FOX.
content: It's here. The Ohio State vs. Michigan trailer dropped Thursday, right on schedule for game week, and it does exactly what a Michigan-week trailer is supposed to do. It reminds you what this game is. And it doesn't ask politely. Ohio State vs. Michigan trailer opens with fire and Buckeye legends The video opens with fire and sparks over helmets. Then the names start flashing across the screen. CJ Barnett. Nolan Baudo. Maurice Clarett. Ryan Day. Archie Griffin. Woody Hayes. James Laurinaitis. Mickey Marotti. Urban Meyer. Jim Tressel. That's the point, and the trailer doesn't hide it. This game belongs to the people who built it. From there it moves fast. Archival footage and recent highlights cut together -- hard hits, touchdowns, celebrations, crowd shots from both sides. The marching band. The Block O. Player close-ups. Campus landmarks. Historical photos. The whole thing is stitched together with voiceover that frames The Game as something bigger than a football game. "The greatest robbery in all of sport." "A vendetta of hatred." "Our culture versus their culture." "For the brotherhood." One line lands harder than the rest. The preparation lasts 364 days. The game lasts 60 minutes. The stadiums, the narration says, are cathedrals built with "blood, sweat, sacrifice." A countdown clock reads "THE GREATEST RIVALRY SINCE OCTOBER 16, 1897." Brick walkways are marked "HATE." And it all ends where it has to end, with three words on the screen and the Block O behind them. FIGHT LIKE HELL. Ohio State vs. Michigan: what the trailer means for Saturday Now, look. A hype video doesn't block anybody. It doesn't cover Jeremiah Smith . It doesn't fix a defense that gave up 31 points at Nebraska . But this one is honest about what Saturday actually is. Ohio State is 7-4. Michigan is 6-5. There is no Big Ten title on the line. There is no College Football Playoff berth on the line. There is only the rivalry, and in this rivalry, that has always been enough. The Buckeyes won in Ann Arbor last year, 27-9, snapping a four-game losing streak in the series. A win Saturday would give Ohio State back-to-back wins over the Wolverines for the first time since 2018-19, and it would do it at home, at noon, in front of a Horseshoe that has been waiting all year for this one. That's what the trailer is selling. Not a playoff run. Not a trophy. Just the game itself, and the 364 days that go into 60 minutes of it. Watch the trailer, then get ready. Saturday can't get here fast enough. title: Tennessee's Arion Carter, DeSean Bishop remain questionable vs Vanderbilt
summary: Tennessee football running back DeSean Bishop and linebacker Arion Carter remain questionable against Vanderbilt.
content: Tennessee football running back DeSean Bishop and linebacker Arion Carter remain questionable against Vanderbilt. Bishop and Carter were listed again on the SEC student-athlete availability report on Nov. 26. It will be updated daily and finalized 90 minutes before the game. No. 7 Tennessee (9-2, 6-2 SEC) must beat Vanderbilt (4-7, 1-7) in the regular-season finale on Nov. 28 (7 p.m. ET, ESPN) to solidify a College Football Playoff spot. Bishop, a Heisman Trophy candidate and Doak Walker Award finalist, suffered a lower-body injury in a 27-13 win over LSU on Nov. 21. He left the game and did not return. Bishop, a former Karns High standout, leads the SEC in rushing with 1,215 yards along with 13 touchdowns. His 248 rushing attempts are second most in the nation. Carter, a former Smyrna High standout, suffered a lower leg injury in a 27-13 win over LSU on Nov. 21. He leads the team with 76 tackles, along with 11 tackles-for-loss, five sacks and three fumble recoveries. Eleven Tennessee players have suffered season-ending injuries in 2026: starting wide receiver Mike Matthews (knee); starting guard Nic Moore (undisclosed medical condition); starting defensive end Tyree Weathersby (knee); starting guard Wendell Moe (lower leg); starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee); starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee); running back Daune Morris (broken leg); safety Dylan Lewis (foot); wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg); linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee); and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body). The initial report is released on Wednesday of an SEC game week, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to kickoff of a Saturday game. Prior to game day, players are designated by their school as available, probable, questionable, doubtful or out for the upcoming game. On game day, they are designated as available, game-time decision or out. Here’s what those designations mean: • Out: Will not play, 0% chance to play. • Doubtful: Unlikely to play, 25% chance to play. • Questionable: Uncertain to play, 50% chance to play. • Probable: Probable to play, 75% chance to play. Per SEC policy, schools must accurately designate players’ participation status. If the school has knowledge that a player may not be able to participate in the upcoming game for any reason (injury, illness, suspension, ineligibility or personal matter), it must report it. Failure to do so will subject schools to potential penalties ranging from $25,000 for a first offense to $100,000 for a third and further offenses. content: Nov. 26—GRAND FORKS — UND forward Josh Zakreski missed four months last season after a practice injury required leg surgery. Zakreski was in and out of the lineup early this season, but landed on UND's top line Saturday night. Zakreski spoke to the Herald about his recovery and shared some of his off-the-ice favorites. Q. Coach Dane Jackson said Saturday night that your injury lingered into the summer and you were unable to skate a lot. What was your summer like? A. I didn't skate from basically when we lost to Wisconsin (in April) until when I came back here in July. I took a lot of time off to try to give my ankle some rest. It seemed to have helped, but I kind of got behind other guys on the team. I've been try to work as hard as I can, skating a lot, getting into the gym and trying to catch up. It kind of seems like I've started to catch back up slowly, so I've been feeling really good on the ice. I'm just kind of excited where I'm going, trending in the right direction. Q. What did it feel like Saturday night on a line with Cole Reschny and Mac Swanson? A. Playing with Resch and Swanny was awesome. Just getting the opportunity to play with those guys. . . they're such gifted hockey players. It was a tight game, but I felt like I played my role well. Q. You beat out a couple of icing calls Saturday. Did it feel like you were playing fast? A. I felt like I had some good momentum. My legs felt really fresh, even though we played Friday. But I felt good out there. I was just trying to use my speed and play my game and play how I was last year before my injury. Q. Why did you start playing hockey? A. Definitely my dad. I started late. I didn't start playing until I was 7 or 8. I was playing floor hockey before. That's what got me into it. I started to enjoy it. Then, my dad put me in skates and I've been in it ever since. Q. If there's one current or former hockey player you could have dinner with, who would you choose? A. This is going to be a weird one, but I'd say Tyson Kozak. I used to room with him in Portland, so I think it would be good to get back and have a nice dinner with him, catch up and see how he's doing. Q. What are your pregame rituals? A. I like to take a nap, for sure. I like to get a good pregame meal in, shower, pretty basic. I would definitely say when I get to the rink, I have a pretty big superstition where I just like to focus on talking to myself and doing a little bit of breath work and visualizing what's going to happen on the ice. Q. What's the most memorable goal you've ever scored? A. I'd say double OT against Everett in the playoffs my last year in Portland. We ended up beating them and they were the top-ranked team in the league that year, so that was my most memorable, for sure. Q. What game was it? A. Game 4. We were down 2-1 in the series. We tied it up, then went to Game 7 of that series and ended up beating them. Q. What's something you're competitive in besides hockey? A. Probably golf. My golf game got a lot better this summer. I was able to shoot my first 80. I almost shot 79, but blew it on the 18th hole. I'd definitely say golf. I'm really starting to get into it. Q. What's your dream vacation spot? A. Somewhere over in Europe like Greece or Italy. . . just somewhere cool I've never really thought about going, somewhere I can enjoy and take a break. I like the food in Italy, so that would be a big one. Q. What's your favorite meme? A. I don't use a whole lot of memes, so I'm not sure I can answer that one. Q. What's your favorite childhood memory? A. Probably playing baseball. My dad and I would always go work in the baseball cages. I managed to hit two home runs in one game, and it kind of taught me that hard work really does pay off. I loved playing baseball growing up. Q. What's the best food spot in Grand Forks? A. I really like that Joe's Italian place. You also can't go wrong with Harry's. Q. If you had to sing karaoke, what would be your go-to song? A. Mr. Saturday Night by Jon Pardi. Q. What's the best meal your mom or dad cook? A. My dad can cook up some good burgers. My mom makes this spaghetti pie. I really like that. She whips up some good pierogies, too. Q. What's your favorite part about your hometown, Saskatoon? A. I'd say seeing my friends and family. I don't get to see them a lot.

title: Cricket Australia widens 'Sandpapergate' forum to 2017-2018 Ashes
summary: Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public.In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0.
content: Australian fielder Cameron Bancroft (R) is questioned by the umpires after using sandpaper in the third Test against South Africa in 2018 (GIANLUIGI GUERCIA) Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public. The governing body has ruled out reopening its investigation into the explosive 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa that blew up again this month. Instead, it proposed a forum for players, coaches and staff on the tour to share their versions of events. In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0. The hosts' consistent ability to get reverse swing in that series had England's bowlers scratching their heads. In the wake of the South Africa fallout, England great Alastair Cook, who was part of the Ashes side, was asked whether the team suspected Australia of ball-tampering. "Yes a little bit, certainly in Perth when the outfield was wet with rain they got the ball-reversing," he said. The issue went no further. Experienced senior counsel Fiona McLeod will lead the forum, which will be open for six weeks and is voluntary. Players' accounts, which can be written or verbal, will be confidential. She will investigate the Ashes, all four Tests of the South Africa tour, the events of March 24, 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught with sandpaper, and the conduct of the 2018 Cricket Australia probe. McLeod will provide a report detailing the principal themes and her recommendations. But what players say will not be published, no new sanctions will come out of it and she is not charged with determining any individual responsibility. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," said Cricket Australia interim chairman David Boon. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn," added Boon. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate." - Reignited - The issue was reignited this month by Usman Khawaja, who claimed in his autobiography that the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball with sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town. He also claimed the practice was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth. A Cricket Australia probe at the time concluded only skipper Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Bancroft were in the know. They were sent home in disgrace and banned for between nine and 12 months. Khawaja's version of events was backed by Warner and Bancroft, but strenuously denied by current captain Pat Cummins and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. The bowling group at the time -- which also included Nathan Lyon -- released a joint statement in 2021 denying any involvement. Cricket Australia last weekend said Cummins had their "unanimous support" to remain Test captain and rejected any suggestion his integrity had been compromised, while praising him for changing the culture of the team. Australia are preparing for four Tests against New Zealand, starting in Perth on December 9. mp/pst

title: Arkansas basketball loses to Michigan State but makes progress
summary: Arkansas didn't get a quality win, but the Hogs seemed to grow up
content: Arkansas basketball lost another game to a power conference opponent on Thursday. The Razorbacks dropped a 70-67 thriller to Michigan State in Detroit. The end result isn't good, but to be quite honest, this was a real step forward for John Calipari's team. It's absolutely true that moral victories are not the point of competition , and that a team with Sweet 16 and maybe Elite Eight potential is still behind schedule for the season, given the lack of high-end wins on its resume. However, given how bad this team looked against Virginia and Indiana, the performance against Tom Izzo's team should be encouraging for John Calipari and his staff. It no longer seems that Arkansas is hopelessly and substantially lost as a team. The defense was a lot better against Michigan State than it was against Indiana. This team needs to be good at the defensive end of the floor in order to be a real contender in the SEC, and the defensive performance on Thanksgiving moves the needle several notches in the right direction. Arkansas forced 13 Michigan State turnovers and blocked 5 shots. Michigan State did shoot over 50 percent, but it wasn't as though the Spartans were getting to the rim with regularity. Michigan State shot the cover off the ball from 3-point range, going 8 of 12. Most opponents aren't going to shoot that well with such a small sample size. Arkansas' effort in this game was excellent. The Hogs collected 17 offensive rebounds to just 7 for Michigan State. Arkansas began to look like the hungry team we hoped it would be before the season began. Michigan State prides itself on hustle and toughness. Arkansas matched Michigan State in that regard, a big sign of growth and evolution for the young Razorbacks. John Calipari really seemed to get through to his young guys on the need to play every possession with passion and forget the previous play. Arkansas was more mature and more forwardly-focused in this game. The players are beginning to understand what it takes to win... but they're not quite there. As good as the effort was for Arkansas, the inability to finish plays is hugely frustrating for the Razorbacks. They hit just 3 of 23 3-point shots. They made only 10 of 16 free throws. Jeremiah Wilkinson and Billy Richmond were a combined 1 for 14 on threes. Arkansas gained Wilkinson in the transfer portal specifically for his offense. As we have said before, if Wilkinson isn't making shots, he's a net negative for this team. Arkansas - which seemed like a deep team on paper before the season began - got just 2 points and 5 rebounds from its bench in 36 total minutes. Arkansas doesn't have the eight- or nine-deep rotation which was supposed to wear down opponents with smothering, constant energy. The better overall performance against Michigan State came from the discovery of the best starting five so far this season, with Davion Thompson starting and Miikka Muurinen going to the bench, two moves we thought Calipari needed to make. The starting five appears to be set, but now the bench needs to give Arkansas a lot more production. The Hogs improved, but now they need to finish off important games against high-quality opponents. It's time to start building an NCAA Tournament resume. Arkansas isn't in a state of full-blown crisis, but the Razorbacks have to start winning the most significant games on their schedule. They can't continue to swing and miss as December arrives.

title: Highlights: MSU basketball dominates second half, tops Arkansas on Thanksgiving
summary: Watch highlights from the Spartans' dominant second half performance to top Arkansas on Thanksgiving in the Motor City
content: Michigan State basketball was a turkey day winner -- but it wasn't easy by any means. The Spartans used a dominant second half performance to rally to a 70-67 victory over Arkansas from the Little Caesars Arena in Detroit on Thanksgiving. The Spartans trailed for a good chunk of the game. But a 24-2 run in the second half gave them the edge that was good enough to pull out the win. Luckily for Michigan State, poor free throw shooting in the final minute didn't haunt them, as a last second three-point attempt from Arkansas bounced out to seal the victory. Michigan State was led by All-American Jeremy Fears Jr., who finished with a double-double at 20 points and 10 assists. Jordan Scott also was a key factor in the win, providing stellar defense and 15 points. The Spartans improve to 6-1 on the year with the win over Arkansas. Michigan State will next play Minnesota on Wednesday. content: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Wes Enis scored 20 points, including five during a decisive late-game stretch, and Creighton beat TCU 95-87 on Thursday in the Players Era 16. The Bluejays (6-1) advance to Friday’s bracket championship against the winner of Baylor and No. 22 Gonzaga after scoring at least 90 points in two straight games for the first time since November 2024. TCU (5-2) erased a nine-point halftime deficit and led 81-80 with 3:43 remaining. Enis answered with a 3-pointer 26 seconds later and added a jumper with 2:32 left to give Creighton an 85-83 lead it never surrendered. Brock Harding converted a three-point play to pull TCU within 87-86 with 1:43 remaining, but Jasen Green blocked Harding’s layup on the Horned Frogs’ next possession. Green made two free throws, and Hudson Greer scored with 42 seconds left to push the lead to 91-87. BJ Davis added 17 points for Creighton, while Greer scored 13 off the bench. Jackson McAndrew and Austin Swartz each had 11. Harding finished with 19 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and four steals for TCU. DJ Thomas scored 17 off the bench, and Micah Robinson added 13 points and seven assists. Creighton shot 55% from the field. Up next TCU: At Notre Dame on Dec. 5. title: Why Rick Barnes says Braeden Lue is on 'monster' run for Tennessee in Las Vegas
summary: Rick Barnes said senior forward Braeden Lue has been "a monster" for Tennessee basketball as it continues rolling defensively with a win vs. Iowa State.
content: LAS VEGAS − In its two wins at the Players Era Festival, Tennessee basketball has held top scorers Pharrel Payne, who entered the tournament averaging 19.6 points per game for Maryland , to five points, and Trey Singleton, averaging 18.6 points for Iowa State, to eight. And after the Vols dispatched the Cyclones with more suffocating defense at Michelob ULTRA Arena on Nov. 26, sophomore forward DeWayne Brown II said there’s one reason why even those talented forwards struggled to put the ball in the basket. “We put B-Lue on ‘em,” he said. “B-Lue” is Braeden Lue, the 6-foot-8, 243-pound transfer from Kennesaw State who logged eight rebounds, three blocks, a steal and more solid individual defense that went beyond the box score as No. 11 Tennessee (7-0) won 75-64 against Iowa State (4-2) on Nov. 26. By beating Iowa State, the Vols have advanced to the third round of the Players Era Festival, where they'll meet the winner of No. 13 St. John's vs. No. 23 Louisville on Nov. 27 (9 p.m. ET, ESPN). A win over the Red Storm or Cardinals would send them to the event's championship game on Nov. 28 (10:30 p.m. ET, ESPN). Lue was an important reason why the Vols dominated defensively against the Cyclones, holding them to 30.6% shooting, the second-lowest by a Tennessee opponent this season, and 0.928 points per possession. “Tremendous,” Tennessee coach Rick Barnes said. “Lue just gives us that physicality. He competes. He's put together a run here four or five games where he's just been really a monster for us on the glass and doing the dirty work. “And he can defend. … We hope he can continue to build because we think he'll be able to guard anybody on the court eventually.” In only 19 minutes per game this season, Lue has excelled at finishing possessions with a defensive rebound, something Tennessee has struggled mightily to do consistently. And he has become a tone-setter for the strong defensive performances which have powered the Vols’ seven-game winning streak that opened this season. “He’s just a junkyard dog. He’s an everyday guy. He knows his role. He knows what he has to do to get us to the next level and he’s really answering that challenge right now,” sophomore guard Jalen Haralson said. “So he’s a guy that we can switch at the four, on smaller guards, big guys. He’s a junkyard dog.” In two preseason exhibitions and the first three games of the regular season, the Vols looked incapable of meeting the high defensive standards Barnes has set during his tenure as coach. Now, they are on a roll, playing a brand of defense that more closely resembles successful Vols teams of the past. Tennessee has allowed opponents to shoot only 26.9% from the field and score 56.5 points per game during a four-game stretch that began with the record-setting victory over Michigan State in Knoxville on Nov. 17. “I think what happened (in the exhibition) at Duke was probably the best thing that ever happened to us, because in that game, we just thought we were just going to shoot the ball and we got embarrassed,” Barnes said. “And after that, we've been on an uptick and we've got a chance to be so much better, too.” Lue’s counting stats during this stretch have been modest - two points, 4.5 rebounds and 0.75 blocks over 18 minutes per game. But his teammates and Barnes insist that Lue has been as crucial to the team’s early success on defense as anyone. Brown is far from surprised with Lue’s steady contributions, because this is what the Vols get from him all the time. “He’s basically doing what he does in practice every day,” Brown said. “He’s just translating it to the game.” Stephen Thompson covers Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball. title: Marlins Need Imanaga After Sánchez Deal, Not Just Any Veteran
summary: The Marlins signed Gary Sánchez to a one-year, $6.5 million deal. Now the front office must target Shota Imanaga to fix a rotation that lacks depth.
content: Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Miami Marlins finally made a move this offseason by agreeing to terms with catcher Gary Sánchez on a one-year contract. A person with knowledge of the talks told The Associated Press the deal could be worth up to $6.5 million. No position player has ever received a larger contract from Peter Bendix, the president of baseball operations, in his tenure. Sánchez, who turns 34 next week, spent last season with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He hit just .209 for the title-winning club but posted a much better .801 OPS against left-handed pitching. The Marlins struggled mightily against southpaws last year, ranking 27th in wRC+ and posting an 85 wRC+ in that category. Sánchez brings a right-handed bat to a lineup that desperately needs to hit lefties better in 2027. Signing Sánchez fixes a specific hole, but it leaves the rotation wide open for a major upgrade. The front office cannot stop there if they want to build on an 80-win season. Sandy Alcantara remains the ace, and Eury Pérez showed flashes of brilliance despite an up-and-down year. Max Meyer is expected to be ready for spring training after a neck injury cut his season short. Beyond those three, the depth is thin. Janson Junk and Ryan Gusto proved serviceable, while Tyler Phillips struggled with home runs after joining the rotation. The team needs a left-handed starter who can eat innings and keep runners off base. Robbie Ray or Matthew Boyd could work as one-year stopgaps, but they are not the long-term answer. Why Imanaga Is The Missing Piece Shota Imanaga is the name the Marlins should chase to complement their young core. He has posted season ERAs of 2.91, 3.73, and 3.77 in his three seasons stateside. His ability to limit traffic on the bases is elite, with a 1.038 WHIP that ranks sixth-lowest among 36 pitchers with at least 80 starts since 2024. Fish On First reported that Imanaga has been a quality starter despite concerns about his tendency to give up the long ball. Preventing walks becomes his greatest strength when he keeps the ball in the park, with walk rates ranking in the 97th, 96th, and 95th percentiles. Preventing walks is exactly what a young rotation needs to stay out of trouble early in games. The Defense Factor And Roster Math While Sánchez offers offensive help, his defense remains a liability. He graded out as a below-average defensive catcher, recording negative six blocks above average and negative two framing. This is why the team added three catchers to the 40-man roster, including Joe Mack and Agustín Ramirez. Sánchez will likely DH or serve as a late-game pinch-hitter against left-handed pitchers. The Marlins might utilize him at first base to enhance their defense, where he has recorded a minus-one DRS. The signing gives the team a veteran presence in a young clubhouse, but it does not solve the starting pitching gap. To become legit contenders, the Marlins must immediately focus on addressing their rotation. Jeff Passan of ESPN reported the agreement on Wednesday night, setting the stage for the next big move.

title: Marlins Outfielder is Generating Trade Interest
summary: Teams around Major League Baseball may want to make serious offers for Miami outfielder Kyle Stowers
content: The Miami Marlins may have another difficult offseason decision on their hands, and this time it involves one of the most productive players in their lineup. Outfielder Kyle Stowers is reportedly generating interest from several clubs, sending rumors swirling that the team may trade him this winter. For a franchise continuing to build toward sustained contention, Stowers represents an interesting asset. He has demonstrated the ability to provide legitimate power in the middle of a lineup, but his growing value could also make him an attractive trade chip as the Marlins evaluate their roster and long-term organizational priorities. The interest is hardly surprising, and president of baseball operations Peter Bendix has taken notice. Stowers enjoyed a breakout 2025 campaign, batting .288 with 25 home runs and 73 RBI in 117 games. However, his 2026 season wasn't quite as impressive, but it shouldn't be overlooked. The youngster hit .239 with 21 home runs and 65 RBI while posting a .789 OPS, which were still solid numbers. Unfortunately, injuries have become a significant part of the conversation surrounding Stowers. He missed the first 21 games of the 2026 season with a hamstring injury, then another hamstring issue and an abdominal strain that limited him to 121 games. There is also the financial component to consider. Stowers is entering his first season of arbitration eligibility, with his 2027 salary projected to be around $3.2 million. He remains under team control through 2029, giving an acquiring club multiple seasons of relatively affordable production. Why Would Miami Trade Him? The Marlins have made it clear that their intention is to become competitive in 2027. After finishing 80-82, the organization is looking to take another step forward rather than dismantle the roster. At the same time, Miami also has several areas that need attention, particularly its pitching staff. If another organization presents an attractive package featuring controllable starting pitching or high-end prospects, Peter Bendix would have to at least consider the possibility. The Marlins have also reportedly explored adding a starting-caliber player at a corner infield or outfield position. Depending on how those discussions develop, Stowers could become somewhat expendable, particularly if Miami identifies an opportunity to improve multiple areas of its roster through a trade. Stowers is only 28, has demonstrated legitimate middle-of-the-order potential, and already has experience producing at an All-Star level. Finding a replacement via free agency could be considerably more expensive, and there is no guarantee that an outside acquisition would provide an upgrade. Unless another club makes an offer that substantially exceeds what Miami believes Stowers can provide over the next several seasons, keeping him might be the smarter baseball decision. In the end, the team must decide if some of the prospects in the organization, like rising star Dillon Lewis , could replace Stowers. Then, the more experienced and (somewhat) established player could be used as a commodity for pitching or perhaps some corner infield help. In that scenario, Bendix would have to pull the trigger. So, in many ways, it may be less about Stowers' ability and potential, and more about the teams needs and the talent the depth they have in the organization. This potential trade comes down to that type of numbers game.

title: Yankees could be in trouble with catcher market drying up
summary: The Yankees can take a marker to their offseason whiteboards.
content: The Yankees can take a marker to their offseason whiteboards. Cross out Tyler Stephenson, who agreed to return to the Reds. Put an “X” through Gary Sánchez, who will sign with the Marlins . Already erased was Ryan Jeffers, who surprisingly accepted the Twins’ qualifying offer. Access the Yankees beat like never before Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees. Try it free The names, while still plentiful in number, grow less intriguing by the day. After spending two seasons without a true righty-hitting option at catcher, the Yankees still are searching for Austin Wells’ complement. “If we can find a good-defending, right-handed-hitting option to level up, that’d be great,” Yankees general manager Brian Cashman said earlier this month at the GM Meetings, “but that’s also slim pickings.” The pickings are even slimmer now. The one catcher still on the free-agent market likely to command a multiyear and not-insignificant contract is Carson Kelly. It is likely that the caliber of catcher the Yankees add will depend upon their pursuits of bullpen, center field and third base help. If they land reliever Adrian Morejon, for example, they probably would reach into the bargain bin elsewhere (unless they bring in a catcher through trade). With less than a week to go before signings and trades are expected to freeze, here are some of the righty-hitting catcher options who are still available through free agency: Carson Kelly: The best still on the board, Kelly likely expects more playing time and a better contract than the Yankees are willing to give. But a veteran, well-regarded catcher with a lifetime .822 OPS against southpaws would fit well. Austin Hedges: One of the premier framers in baseball, the 34-year-old always has been defensively excellent but not much of an offensive threat. Last season, he did hit lefties well (.747 OPS). Carson Kelly watches the action during the Cubs’ loss to the Marlins on Sept. 22, 2026, at Wrigley Field in Chicago. Getty Images James McCann: A veteran and former Met who has settled nicely into a part-time/backup role in the twilight of his career, McCann’s defense has slipped, but he has hit decently — although last season, he was stronger against righty pitching. Kyle Higashioka: Another for the run-it-back Yankees? Higashioka, now 36, has seen his pop time slow, and he caught just seven of 39 attempted base stealers last season, but he remains agile behind the plate and hit lefties well last season before suffering a flexor strain in July. Elias Díaz: His defense still was solid during his age-35 season with the Royals and Rangers this past year and he posted an .820 OPS against southpaws. Do the Yankees want a slugger with nice pop but poor on-base skills? Kyle Higashioka steps up to the plate during a Yankees-Tigers game on Sept. 7, 2023, at the Stadium. Getty Images And possible trade candidates: Iván Herrera/Pedro Pagés: The Cardinals are deep at catcher, where Leo Bernal likely will start next season after a strong debut and with top prospect Rainiel Rodríguez on the way. They could afford to part with the bat-first Herrera or glove-first Pagés. Herrera mostly served as DH last season, struggling particularly behind the plate with holding opposing base runners, but he owns an .863 OPS against lefties in his five seasons. Pagés has not hit much in his three years but is a strong defender. Freddy Fermin/Luis Campusano: After top prospect Ethan Salas got his feet wet last season, the Padres have a surplus of catchers. The 31-year-old Fermin is defensively strong but owns only a .599 OPS over his past two seasons. Campusano’s all-around defense has made strides, particularly his throwing arm, and he is coming off a strong season in which he hit .265 with a .795 OPS. Agustín Ramírez: With Sánchez landing in Miami as a complement to Joe Mack, would the Marlins shop Ramírez? Maybe not; they could store the former Yankees prospect in the minors and work on his defense, which has been weak. But the 25-year-old slugger, who went from the Yankees to the Marlins in the Jazz Chisholm Jr. trade, has a strong offensive reputation and has posted a .755 OPS against lefties in his two major league seasons.

title: Dricus Du Plessis: If the Adesanya I fought shows up at UFC Riyadh, Magomedov 'done for'
summary: Dricus Du Plessis expects Israel Adesanya to rebound at UFC Fight Night 295.
content: Dricus Du Plessis expects Israel Adesanya to rebound at UFC Fight Night 295. Former champion Adesanya (24-6 MMA, 13-6 UFC) takes on rising middleweight Shara Magomedov (17-1 MMA, 6-1 UFC) in the Dec. 5 main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Adesanya will look to snap a four-fight losing skid – one of the setbacks which came in a title fight against Du Plessis at UFC 305 . Although Adesanya hasn't been getting his hand raised, he has shown shades of his championship form, and that's what Du Plessis is banking on. "It's an awesome fight, and once again with Adesanya, that's what's so great in his whole career: He's not shying away from anything," Du Plessis told Fight Forecast . "He's still taking those hard fights. 'Bullet' is an up-and-coming killer. I honestly believe Adesanya, I hope for him, and I just believe he's going to be too much for Shara because Shara 'Bullet' can do great things and he can strike, but if the Adesanya that fought me gets in there, Shara 'Bullet' is done for. Adesanya, he changed teams, so he's going to have a chip on his shoulder. "He went to go and train with (Alexander Volkanovski), and we've seen what Volk has been doing. That team has been really shaping up so, big ups to Adesanya. At the end of his career, he doesn't need to fight these killers and to change the gym now at this age and at the end of his career. He doesn't have to do that. But he's such a martial artist, he wants to be the best he can be, and the fact that he does that shows me that he's still committed to winning, not just competing. I'm excited for it, and I'm going with Izzy for that one." Adesanya parted ways with his longtime gym, City Kickboxing, to train in a more concentrated environment at Unity MMA. Du Plessis was asked if the UFC still needs Adesanya. "Right now he's almost in that Anderson Silva time in his career, at the end where Anderson was losing fights, but nobody cared," Du Plessis said. "His legacy was already cemented. He's done what he's needed for the sport, and right now I don't think the UFC needs him. I think fans love him, fans love his style, and I think he loves the sport, so I don't think it's the UFC needs him anymore. "I think he loves it so much he needs it more – not that he needs it. He needs it for himself. He loves it so much that he feels empty without it. I think that's how a lot of us feel. ... I think if he gets that big, big win, I think maybe even this fight he might call it a day. But up until, let the man fight. Let him enjoy his life because it's not like he's getting manhandled, and he's fighting the best in the world." title: Will Anderson Jr. Named AFC Defensive Player of the Week, Continues to Set the Tone for Houston
summary: The league-leading pass rusher dominated Indianapolis to secure his second career weekly honor, proving he is a generational centerpiece fueling DeMeco Ryans’ elite defensive transformation in Houston.
content: If there is one thing Houston Texans fans can appreciate about Will Anderson Jr., it's that the man understands the assignment. Being named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week is another indication that the Texans have something special in their young defensive end. But beyond the individual recognition, this award speaks volumes about what Anderson means to Houston's defensive identity and the culture DeMeco Ryans has been building. For me, Anderson receiving this recognition isn't necessarily a surprise. It's more of a reminder to the rest of the NFL that Houston has a legitimate defensive difference-maker who deserves to be mentioned among the league's elite pass rushers. Will Anderson Jr. is on top for the 7th straight week 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Mp0T1NkNSG — NFL (@NFL) November 24, 2026 Anderson Put the Colts on Notice Coming off Houston's dominant 26-3 Thursday night victory over the Indianapolis Colts, Anderson earned his second career AFC Defensive Player of the Week award after accumulating five tackles, four quarterback hits, two tackles for loss and a sack that resulted in his first career safety. The interesting thing about Anderson's performance is that the stat sheet doesn't necessarily tell the entire story. His presence alone disrupted the offensive rhythm of Indianapolis and made things extremely uncomfortable for quarterback Daniel Jones. Houston surrendered only 167 yards of total offense and 38 rushing yards. The Colts were held scoreless throughout the final three quarters. That's the type of defensive football Texans fans have been waiting to see consistently this season. Anderson was at the forefront of it. More Than Just a Pass Rusher What I appreciate most about Anderson is that he isn't a one-dimensional defensive end. Everybody loves seeing quarterbacks get slammed to the turf, but Anderson's ability to defend the run, collapse the pocket and force opposing quarterbacks into uncomfortable situations makes him extremely valuable. Through 10 games this season, Anderson has registered 44 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and a league-leading 11.5 sacks. He also leads the NFL with 60 quarterback pressures and a pressure rate of 19.3%. Those numbers are ridiculous when you consider the amount of attention opposing offensive coordinators have to dedicate to containing him. When Anderson commands additional blockers, opportunities open up for other members of the defensive front. That pressure also makes life a little easier for Houston's secondary. That's where his impact goes beyond individual statistics. Anderson makes the players around him better, and that's a characteristic you want from a franchise defensive player. Is It Time to Talk Defensive Player of the Year Why not? I think it's time we start having a more serious conversation about Anderson potentially bringing the NFL Defensive Player of the Year award back to Houston. According to the NFL, Anderson joins Von Miller and former Texans great J.J. Watt as the only players since 2000 to produce at least 10 sacks and 15 tackles for loss in three separate seasons before turning 26. That's some pretty impressive company. I'm not necessarily ready to start comparing Anderson's entire career to Watt's, but the trajectory is certainly encouraging. Houston has witnessed what a generational defensive talent can do for a franchise, and Anderson is beginning to establish his own legacy. The biggest factor moving forward will be maintaining that production while helping Houston climb back into playoff contention. Despite the inconsistencies surrounding the Texans this season, Anderson has remained one of the team's most dependable assets. My Two Pennies As a football fan, I thoroughly enjoy watching Anderson because his motor never seems to shut off. Whether he's fighting through a double-team, chasing down a running back or putting pressure on a quarterback, the effort is consistently there. Being named AFC Defensive Player of the Week is well-deserved, but I believe Anderson has his sights set on something much bigger. Now, it's up to the rest of the team to match that energy. Individual accolades are great, but watching Anderson lead this defense into the postseason would make his remarkable 2026 campaign that much sweeter. And quite frankly, I wouldn't be surprised if there's some additional hardware waiting for No. 51 when this season is all said and done.

Jahmyr Gibbs had quite a night on Thursday , but Chicago Bears linebacker TJ Edwards was not going to let the Detroit Lions running back seal the deal in the fourth quarter. With a little over two minutes left in the fourth quarter and the Lions leading by three points, Detroit quarterback Jared Goff threw a short pass to the left to a wide-open Gibbs on a 4th-and-4 at Chicago’s 33. A first-down conversion would have essentially ended the game, but Edwards had other plans, as he tackled Gibbs to force a Lions turnover on downs. title: Cowboys vs. Eagles recap: Dallas embarrassed by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day
summary: The Cowboys are a national embarrassment
content: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys is tackled by Andrew Mukuba #24 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images It will go down in history as one of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient. They are all of the bad things. On a day where we are supposed to be thankful it is hard to find a reason to be for this specific part of our lives. The Dallas Cowboys are a weekly embarrassment and Thursday was the latest example of it. What even happens now? First Quarter The Eagles won the toss and deferred which put the Cowboys offense to work first. Dak Prescott and the group did not waste the opportunity. Javonte Williams was served seconds, thirds, and then some as the team marched down the field, partly thanks to a huge 3rd and 18 conversion from Dak to CeeDee Lamb, but it was Williams who capped it off with the touchdown to give the home team an early 7-0 lead. JAVONTE TD pic.twitter.com/IFq12RHEEy — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Things were looking rather impressive for Joe Milton and the Eagles. I’d imagine that many Cowboys fans were starting to assume a score was happening any minute across the first drive. Thankfully that was not the case. Right around field goal range the Eagles chose to roll the dice on fourth and short… and Quinnen Williams said no! QUINNEN!!! pic.twitter.com/Yz2K1cZsqi — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Weirdly a sequence occurred on the next drive that did the first. Dak Prescott scrambled for a first on a third down, but the gain was negated by a penalty. This brought up third and long (16 here, 18 before) and Prescott connected with a star receiver (George Pickens here, CeeDee Lamb before) for the first down. After that KaVontae Turpin had a stellar catch where he turned on the boosters and reached the endzone in a flash. Dallas was up 14-0 early. TURP TD!!!! pic.twitter.com/8ihtwLzjs2 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The quarter ended with Philly holding the ball right after. Second Quarter The Eagles punted shortly after teams flipped the field which put the Cowboys offense back up. Given that they were already leading 14-0 this was a chance to really blow things open. Unfortunately they could not and wound up punting the ball for the first time in a while. A big 3rd and 12 conversion from Philadelphia put them within striking distance and while they were unable to fully get home they did give Jake Elliott a chance at a 48-yard field goal. It was good and the visitors had their first points on the day. The Cowboys offense did not miss this time around. KaVontae Turpin was involved again, this time on a jet sweep, and there was a big conversion from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb. But it was Javonte Williams who cased in yet again. This marked his second score on the day and gave Dallas a 21-3 lead. JAVONTE WILLIAMS AGAIN pic.twitter.com/mbe4qovd3I — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The dam finally broke, though. Joe Milton had been showing moments of promise to this point in the game and at long last he delivered. It was a classic Joe Milton throw… meaning it traveled quite a long ways. JOE MILTON'S ARM TALENT IS RIDICULOUS 🎯 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2MLAir7i29 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 The Cowboys received the ball with just over four minutes to go. It felt like an important possession as it would likely be their last one before the half and they received the ball to start the game. Points were essential. In all honesty it was a pretty penalty-filled drive. Officials were calling them left and right, many of them helping the Cowboys, but Dallas was moved back after an apparent touchdown to Brevyn Spann-Ford. On third and goal from the 12-yard line… Dak Prescott found Javonte Williams for a score to close the half. It also marked a hat trick of scores on the day for Williams specifically. JAVONT3 pic.twitter.com/9lMQ1ebII8 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took a knee and it was Miranda Lambert time. Third Quarter Philadelphia went three and out to start the second half which is always great to see. The Cowboys took the field and once again with an opportunity to stretch their lead. Dallas punted it back themselves. This game truly felt over, but obviously with a lot of time left that was not the case in any real way. Football had to be played. Shemar James sacked Joe Milton which helped to ensure the punt streak continued. Philly booted it back and the Cowboys offense returned to the field. It was a little bit of the same for the Cowboys offense in terms of not being able to fully convert. They did score, but only 3 points by way of Brandon Aubrey. This was notable though as it was a 59-yard field goal that he drilled with ease which was great to see given how this season has gone. The FOX broadcast also noted that this was the longest ever field goal made on Thanksgiving all-time. Pretty neat. The third quarter ended right as Philadelphia crossed the 50-yard line… and then Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith again to get another touchdown on the board with 15 seconds left. It was suddenly 31-17, good guys. Fourth Quarter Things did not go particularly well for the Cowboys offense to start the fourth quarter. They faced a fourth and short on their side of the field and left the offense on the field. It was bold, but nobody really thought they were going to run a play. Thankfully they just fished for offsides and punted. Or so we thought. The Cowboys tried to punt… but it was blocked and returned for a Philly touchdown. Out of nowhere it was 31-24 with basically the entire fourth quarter left. EAGLES BLOCKED PUNT TD PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1mrM5lDeTK — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 It goes without saying that the pressure was high. The Cowboys were on the verge of blowing this game. Something had to happen. Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb specifically played like that was the case. They hooked up for a pair of big gains along the drive and then Dak put the exclamation point on things himself by running it on for a touchdown… thanks to some serious hops. DAK!!!! pic.twitter.com/1GdrVEJ8Ls — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 27, 2026 It seemed like this was going to essentially end the game. Have you seen the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, though Philadelphia traveled 42 yards in 3 plays to match the touchdown. Joe Milton literally did by rushing it in himself. Joe Milton takes it in himself! PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ERZiu9S8Kr — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 The Eagles missed the two-point conversion so it was 38-30 Cowboys. In the blink of an eye it was 3rd and 14 right past the team’s own 15-yard line. It appeared as if the Cowboys had pulled off something truly incredible. Dak Prescott found George Pickens for a modest gain, but then he threw a lateral across the field to Hunter Luepke and the fullback took it all the way to the house. He even jumped into the Salvation Army kettle. Unfortunately it was deemed to be a forward pass from Pickens and therefore a penalty which resulted in the loss of the down. Bryan Anger successfully got the punt off this time and the Eagles returned it past midfield. There was still half the fourth quarter remaining. It was then that the Cowboys defense made a play. On third and forever they picked off Joe Milton. Cobie Durant was the hero in question. COBIE DURANT pic.twitter.com/1WmfLgtNqk — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 27, 2026 You would think that this would have given the Cowboys the opportunity to ice the game. You would think that the offense that had been on fire for so long would have scored to fully put things away. They wound up settling for a field goal attempt from 40 yards out. Brandon Aubrey missed. It was unbelievable. Dak's reaction to Aubrey's missed field goal. 📺 FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/PCmN1dFmj9 — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) November 27, 2026 Fine. Mistakes happen. Surely the Cowboys defense would lock in. It took the Eagles just 4 plays to travel 70 yards and score. Seriously. Given the failed two-point conversion earlier though the Eagles had to have one here. They failed again so Dallas retained a slim lead at 38-36. The Cowboys got past midfield. In fact, they got all the way to the Philadelphia 39-yard line. They were facing 4th and 1. Instead of letting Brandon Aubrey try a field goal, he had just missed obviously, the Cowboys chose to go for it. Dak Prescott was sacked. It felt grim. You know what happened. The Eagles pulled off a 60-yard field goal to win 39-38. The Cowboys’ season is over. Unbelievable.

title: Eagles mount furious comeback, beat Cowboys 39-38 in Thanksgiving classic
summary: What looked like a blowout turned into a great one, as Philadelphia stormed back to win in Dallas.
content: It was a Thanksgiving Day classic in Dallas. In a wild game that went from an apparent blowout to a thrilling comeback, the Cowboys jumped out to a 31-10 lead and then lost 39-38 when Eagles kicker Jake Elliott hit a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton played by far the best game of his career, throwing for 331 yards, with three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. We've always known Milton had a strong arm, but he showed today that he's more than just a thrower. He can lead an NFL offense as a quarterback. But Dak Prescott is a good quarterback, too, and he turned in a big game of his own. He threw for 291 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Prescott's favorite receiver was CeeDee Lamb, who finished with 134 receiving yards, and running back Javonte Williams ran for two touchdowns and also caught a touchdown pass. The Eagles, however, got a monster game from wide receiver DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns. Smith was sensational while the Eagles were coming back in the fourth quarter. Special teams miscues killed the Cowboys: The Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown, and Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Aubrey, who became the highest-paid kicker in the NFL this offseason, is having the worst season of his career. The loss drops the Cowboys to 5-7 and is devastating to their playoff hopes. The 4-7 Eagles aren't contenders, but they played like contenders today.

title: ‘That was freaking insane’: Chicago Bears stay ‘super resilient’ to rally and pull off a 39-35 win
summary: When Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze toe-tapped in the end zone for a 6-yard go-ahead touchdown catch with 3 seconds left Thursday, it transported Sam Roush back to the frenzied fourth-quarter rallies of last season — and the rookie tight end wasn’t even on the team then. “I remember being in college (at Stanford) watching (the Bears) last year and being like, ‘How is this even ...
content: When Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze toe-tapped in the end zone for a 6-yard go-ahead touchdown catch with 3 seconds left Thursday, it transported Sam Roush back to the frenzied fourth-quarter rallies of last season — and the rookie tight end wasn’t even on the team then. “I remember being in college (at Stanford) watching (the Bears) last year and being like, ‘How is this even possible?’” he said after the Bears’ 39-35 comeback thriller over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day at Ford Field. “And now I get to be a part of it.” Odunze’s score was the first time the Bears led all game. “Obviously, I’m not the guy that made those big plays today, but seeing Rome do that was incredible at the end of the game,” Roush said. “And (quarterback) Caleb (Williams), like, that’s why they call Caleb ‘Ice Man.’ Like, that was freaking insane. “We just got some dogs in the game.” If there’s a word that describes the Bears on Thursday, it’s “dogged.” There were several points in the game that looked like backbreakers, and some of the setbacks that seemed almost insurmountable. • Midway through the first quarter, tight end Colston Loveland lost a fumble after his only catch. • Later in the first, the Bears lost Loveland for the rest of the game after he injured his knee while blocking on a run play. • The Bears’ chance to mount a 2-minute drill before halftime ended with Williams taking a strip-sack and a safety. • When Jahmyr Gibbs sprinted 70 yards for a fourth-quarter touchdown, it looked like a wrap. Bears running back D’Andre Swift said they remained unfazed, even as the Lions built an 11-point advantage after Gibbs’s scamper pushed Detroit’s lead to 35-24 with 8 minutes, 20 seconds left in the game. “We (were) always in the game, and I feel like the game never really got away from us,” Swift said. “We gave up some stuff early on and kind of made it hard for us. “But it was a heavyweight fight. Back and forth, back and forth. Went down to the wire.” Swift had a 30-yard touchdown run, and Kyle Monangai ran in 1- and 2-yard touchdowns, scores that helped keep the Bears engaged in a seesaw battle in the second and third quarters. Odunze’s two touchdown receptions both came in the fourth quarter. The Bears defense coughed up 205 rushing yards and three touchdowns to Gibbs, but also came up with a pair of crucial plays. “Defense came up in critical situations,” Swift said. “It’s how we fight as a team. “That’s the one word I would use for that win is just ‘fight.’” Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman caught his third interception of the season (and second in consecutive games) after Jared Goff’s fourth-quarter pass bounced off receiver Jameson Williams’ hands and into Thieneman’s chest. The offense couldn’t convert that pick into points, but it didn’t stall a Lions drive that reached the Chicago 34-yard line and likely cost Detroit at least a field goal try. “I felt like that was a big change, and then giving it to the offense and all them to build some more momentum with that,” Thieneman said. “I felt it was really important.” On another crucial defensive play, T.J. Edwards wrangled Gibbs to the ground after a 1-yard catch on fourth-and-4, where nothing was backing up Edwards but a lot of green turf. Edwards’ stop forced the Lions to turn the ball over on downs. The offense then marched 68 yards on 13 plays in 2 minutes, 14 seconds, with Odunze’s toe-drag touchdown capping it off. Like Roush, Thieneman isn’t used to these kinds of wild finishes. “It’s awesome, he said. “Definitely a lot of ups and downs. You gotta control yourself, gotta stay level in it all.” Throughout the game, various players and coaches would make uplifting comments such as “don’t forget we’ve got a game to win, we’re still in this,” Kalif Raymond said. “I remember, I want to say, (quarterbacks coach) J.T. Barrett came out on the sidelines, like, ‘Hey, man, we’re in this. This game is down to the wire.’” Last season, the Bears engineered seven late-game comebacks between the regular season and playoffs. This season, they’ve taken more leads and spent more time fending off comebacks, so Thursday’s game was the first true nailbiter. “Man, I’m really proud of our guys,” Ben Johnson said. “I think about how far we’ve come since we’ve been in the building the last year and a half. Just the professionalism with which they conduct themselves, the hard work they put in all season long, but certainly on a short week like this. “And then the belief that they had in a game like that, particularly when we gave them some momentum at halftime. And yet to be able to weather that storm.” Linebacker D’Marco Jackson said the team had heard the chatter about the Bears’ struggles in the NFC North (2-6 under Johnson heading into the matchup), so to steal a win on the road against a division opponent, under those circumstances, was “super huge.” “I think a lot of people wrote us off thinking we weren’t going to be able to come in here and pull it off,” Jackson said. “We did just that and we put everybody on notice.” Roush also learned about the makeup of the team. “Super resilient,” he said. “Lot of playmakers. … It really is incredible. We’re still hungry.”

title: The J.J. McCarthy improvement that could get Giants to the next level
summary: The deep balls were flying from the right arm of J.J. McCarthy, but the connections were tough to come by.
content: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) passes over Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Travon Walker (44) in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. The deep balls were flying from the right arm of J.J. McCarthy, but the connections were tough to come by. Deep to rookie Malachi Fields, incomplete. Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW Deep to Malik Nabers, incomplete. Deep to Darnell Mooney, incomplete. Another one deep to Fields, interception overturned upon review to an incomplete pass. Deep to Mooney over the middle, incomplete. Yet another deep shot to Mooney on third-and-17, not close, and some boos ensued from the crowd at MetLife Stadium. “At the end of the day, I just missed them,” McCarthy said. “The big thing that kind of stood out to me was just put some more air on the ball and let the receivers be able to track it a little bit better, but that’s an easy fix and we’ll get it fixed.” These down-the-field attempts from McCarthy were part of his 20 incomplete passes in the 23-18 upset victory over the Jaguars, showing that the Giants have to be really good, but not perfect, to beat a quality opponent. McCarthy has been a godsend since arriving in a trade with the Vikings — that 2027 fifth-round pick was draft capital well spent — and he takes a 3-1 record as the Giants starting quarterback into Sunday’s game with the Colts in Indianapolis. Ever since his arrival Sept. 29, it has been a full-speed-ahead crash course for McCarthy, as far as learning a brand-new offense and trying to fast-forward his comfort with the unfamiliar players around him. Building chemistry with wide receivers and tight ends takes time, and that was not on McCarthy’s side. The reputation for having a strong arm and a nice feel for the deep ball preceded McCarthy to his second NFL stop. That is the next bit of firepower to add to his arsenal as the Giants look to secure and build on their first-place lead in the NFC East. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) passes over Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Travon Walker (44) in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Adam Hunger “For me, personally, just having more time on task with my guys being able to hit the ones that are there, especially the deeper shots,” McCarthy said. “Just being able to get in here and work with the guys just constantly and just be able to get those reps over and over again. “But I’m going to make those. Those are things that are going to come and have shown up, but sometimes you just miss. In this league, you can’t miss too many times. So just being able to be ready for that next opportunity and nail it.” McCarthy has not pushed the ball into the end zone as often as the Giants would like. He has only two touchdown passes in his four starts. Some of this is happenstance — the Giants had four rushing touchdowns in McCarthy’s first start, a 27-21 overtime victory in Houston. Some of this is McCarthy at times still looking a bit uncertain within the offense, as far as going through his progressions. Making the timely throw, and finding a way to win, though, are McCarthy hallmarks. That is how he went 27-1 at Michigan. His stats were often mid-level — the Wolverines were largely a running team during his time in Ann Arbor — but when a throw or a run was needed to keep a drive alive, McCarthy delivered with impressive regularity. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) speaks at a press conference in East Rutherford, N.J., Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post McCarthy was spraying the ball down the stretch against the Jaguars as the Giants fell into a second-half rut, with four consecutive possessions failing to pick up a first down. When it came time to close out the game or else hand it back over to Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars offense, McCarthy came through with his most clutch throw. He wanted to find Nabers on the left side, but Nabers was shadowed by two defenders. No opening there. McCarthy instantly pivoted and fired a strike to Fields for a 19-yard completion. That alleviated a great deal of pressure. After two 5-yard runs from Cam Skattebo, McCarthy could kneel down three times to end it. “That was my second read,’’ McCarthy said of the pass to Fields. “There are so many things that you could really look at from your perspective and everyone has — they’re entitled to their own perspective and their own opinion, but if you’re not really in the room and you don’t understand what the progressions are. Sometimes it’s zone-based or man-based coverage reads where it’s like, yeah, it might be your first progression, but it’s really the second in your thought process of what the defense has given you. It’s little things like that where you just can’t really focus on and just got to worry about doing your job as a quarterback, which is throwing to the open guy, and sometimes, a lot of the times, with good defenses, that is going through your reads.” And, sometimes, those reads lead to deep throws down the field. “Come back and make the next throw, and that’s a confident guy, and he’s been in a lot of huge games,” coach John Harbaugh said. “And we’re going to start hitting some of those deep passes. We wanted to take some shots, we wanted to go after them downfield and we did, and those are going to start happening. We’ll start making those plays for sure.”

title: NFL Under Fire After Refs’ Controversial Call Wipes Out Eagles TD Following Javonte Williams Fumble During Cowboys Clash
summary: An officiating decision in the Eagles-Cowboys game has put the NFL’s review process under scrutiny again. Philadelphia’s touchdown, which came after a Javonte Williams fumble, was taken off the board by the officials, and the play never counted.
content: LANDOVER, MD – DECEMBER 25: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams 33 reads his blockers during game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Washington Commanders on December 25, 2025 at Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD. Photo by Charles Brock/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA DEC 25 Cowboys at Commanders EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon251225004 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire An officiating decision in the Eagles-Cowboys game has put the NFL’s review process under scrutiny again. Philadelphia’s touchdown, which came after a Javonte Williams fumble, was taken off the board by the officials, and the play never counted. The officials’ interpretation of forward progress is disputed; some analysts argue Williams did fumble before being ruled down. Nevertheless, the ruling has now prompted fans and analysts to question how the rule was applied and whether the league enforces it consistently across games. “Whistle halts Riq Woolen return after Javonte Williams fumble. Nick Sirianni protested the early stoppage,” Wire Report NFL posted on X . Williams was driving toward the end zone when the ball came loose just short of the goal line in the second quarter. Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen scooped it up and took off for a 97-yard return that looked like a touchdown. Before he got there, the whistle blew. The officials ruled that Williams’ forward progress had already been stopped, which meant the play was dead before Woolen reached the end zone, preventing a TD rather than erasing one. When a touchdown gets erased in a rivalry game, the entire playoff picture shifts. Stay ahead of every controversial call and its impact with EssentiallySports NFL coverage. That ruling carries a harsh consequence, because forward progress calls can’t be challenged. Nick Sirianni had nothing to throw a flag over and no review to ask for, so the Eagles simply had to line up again. Dallas then scored its own touchdown to build the halftime cushion. By the start of the fourth quarter, the Cowboys led 31-17, with Philadelphia having added ten points in the second quarter and seven in the third. The officials’ call on it is now drawing heavy criticism. One fan, whose comment was originally in Spanish, summed up how it looked from the stands: “To me, this was a fumble by Javonte Williams and a potential defensive TD for the Eagles that would have made it 21-17 at halftime. The refs blew the whistle (too early, in my opinion), and that killed the play. Anyway… on to the next one.” Media voices were just as direct. Former ESPN writer Ed Werder pointed to how plays like this are usually handled: “That was a quick whistle on the potential Javonte Williams fumble and Eagles recovery. They usually allow that to play out through the return. Riq Woolen was stopped from a 98-yard return by whistle. Nick Sirianni had a legit argument and made it.” Eagles reporter Brandon Lee Gowton was far less diplomatic, as he said on X, “Absolute horseshit ruling on that Javonte Williams fumble creates a 14-point swing in the Cowboys’ favor. Abysmal officiating.” Interestingly, the frustration wasn’t limited to Philadelphia’s side. Cowboys beat reporter Joseph Hoyt saw it the same way. “They’re going to say his forward progress is stopped, but Javonte Williams did fumble that, it was a clear recovery, and Tariq Woolen took it back for a TD. Cowboys catch a HUGE break,” Hoyt wrote on X. Fan comments piled up too. One take captured the mood of the Eagles faithful. “Eagles fans feel robbed 😤 Philly appeared to rip the ball from Javonte Williams near the goal line, but officials ruled his forward progress was stopped, and the call wasn’t reviewable. #FlyEaglesFly” And one fan directed his anger straight at the league’s officiating account. :@NFLOfficiating enough of this garbage of a product you have out there. Fine them, fire them, do something!”, a fan wrote. A call that can’t be reviewed leaves nothing but the debate, and this one will be argued for a long time. title: Recent opponents reportedly spill truth about Patriots 'soft' defense
summary: The Patriots' defense was reportedly called "soft" by recent opponents.
content: The perception from some of the New England Patriots' recent opponents is that the defensive unit is "soft." That's a major turnaround for a unit that was considered one of the best in the NFL last season. With that said, the Patriots have given up 99 points in total over the last three games. That includes 35 points against the Detroit Lions and 45 points against the Green Bay Packers. There really is no sugar-coating the fact that it has looked like a disaster at times against top-tier offensive teams. Even worse, those other teams are starting to talk about it. "I've had conversations with people that have played the Patriots of late, and that is a word that has come up about their defense is soft," Perry said on Zolak & Bertrand . "And softer than what they were anticipating I think, too, because you have some big names, especially up front there like in the interior and the way they were moved in that Lions game I think surprised a lot of people." The defensive front has struggled to stop the run and get home consistently enough to impact opposing quarterbacks. However, one of the more disappointing problems for the Patriots has been their defensive backfield. Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez hasn't played up to his potential, and Carlton Davis Davis hasn't been available due to injury. Kevin Byard has also struggled at safety. There is also the fact that defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr hasn't been as effective as a play-caller as he was a year ago. Overall, it has been a frustrating season for a defensive unit that came into the year with high expectations. The good news is that there is still time left to turn things around with the hardest stretch of football still ahead. Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook . title: ‘He’s a Strange Guy,’ ‘The One Thing You Don’t Do’ — Steelers Legend Terry Bradshaw Doesn’t Mince Words About Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy Drama
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw picked a side in the Aaron Rodgers saga, and it was Mike McCarthy’s. Bradshaw minced no words on FOX’s Thanksgiving pregame show on Thursday.
content: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers and Terry Bradshaw Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw picked a side in the Aaron Rodgers saga, and it was Mike McCarthy’s. Bradshaw minced no words on FOX’s Thanksgiving pregame show on Thursday. He stood with McCarthy, the head coach, and the Rooney family a day after the Steelers released Rodgers, who had leveled a string of accusations at McCarthy on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Terry Bradshaw Faults the Way Aaron Rodgers Left Pittsburgh Bradshaw began with the Rooneys and McCarthy, and he was open about his own ties: “Growing up in that family, the Rooney family especially, I would say this: they’re a classy, classy bunch, classy organization. Mike McCarthy and I have been friends for years. Classy man. I don’t know all the details. … I’m sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. … Am I surprised? Absolutely not. To my opinion, he’s a strange guy anyway.” Notably, the heart of his criticism was how Rodgers went about leaving: “And the one thing you don’t do—all of us athletes up here, including you, none of us turn on our teammates. We don’t turn on our coaching staff. We don’t turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out. Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that.” He also turned to something he remembered Rodgers saying about life after Pittsburgh: “And one thing I’m reminded of. He said, when my—when I’m through playing here in Pittsburgh, I’ll disappear and you’ll never hear or see from me again. And I hope this is one time he’s telling the truth.” Bradshaw was reacting to a whirlwind few days in Pittsburgh. The Steelers benched Rodgers for Mason Rudolph on Tuesday night, ahead of Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. On Wednesday, Rodgers went on McAfee’s show and accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and skipping others, along with team events. Rodgers was indeed blunt about where he stood on the benching and the play-calling: “If you try and bench me or don’t change the play-calling, then you should just release me, because I feel like, at this point, I’m doing what’s right for the organization.” RUN YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Ultimate GM Simulator McCarthy, who made the call to bench Rodgers, met reporters later Wednesday and kept the details to himself, though he called what Rodgers had made an “ultimatum.” Incidentally, the Steelers cut Rodgers the same day. Meanwhile, team president Art Rooney II made the organization’s position clear on Thursday in an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac: “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond. The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney also pointed to the teammates Rodgers left behind: “There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload. … He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure.” When asked whether he regretted signing Rodgers, Rooney said: “I’m disappointed the way it came out. … But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn’t expecting it to go this way this year.” Rodgers and McCarthy go back a long way. They spent 13 years together in Green Bay, including a Super Bowl XLV win over Pittsburgh, and the Steelers turned to McCarthy after 19 seasons under Mike Tomlin. Rodgers returned this past spring for a second season in Pittsburgh on a one-year contract with $22 million guaranteed. The 42-year-old QB cleared waivers Thursday and is now a free agent. He is 29th in PFN’s QB Impact Rankings with a grade of 67.2. Rodgers has said 2026 will be his final NFL season, though he has not said whether he intends to sign with another team for the remainder of it.
