title: Stunner! Eagles rally from 21 down to beat Cowboys 39-38. 4 takeaways
summary: The Eagles rallied from 21 points down late in the third quarter to beat the Dallas Cowboys 39-38
content: ARLINGTON, Texas − It took 10 games, but finally, the Eagles ' offense had by far the output of the season, with quarterback Joe Milton throwing two long touchdown passes to DeVonta Smith, one for 50 yards and the other for 45. The Eagles also blocked a punt and recovered the ball for a touchdown. They needed all of it, including a 60-yard field goal by Jake Elliott with 2 seconds left as they rallied from 21 points down late in the third quarter to stun the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 on Nov. 26. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets The Eagles had scored their most points in any game this season, by far, as embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and the offense finally showed its potential. And that was with running back Saquon Barkley and tight end Dallas Goedert leaving in the first quarter with injuries. The Eagles fell behind 21-3 midway through the second quarter, and 31-10 with 3:35 left late in the third quarter. That's when the Eagles finally got the offense going, or at least figured out that their best play was simply to throw the ball deep to Smith. The Eagles' star wide receiver finished with a career-high 200 yards receiving on 11 catches, to go along with two touchdowns. Milton, making only his third career start, went 21-for-31 for 331 yards with 3 TDs and an interception. Milton and Smith's first connection came with 4:06 left in the first half with the Eagles at midfield. Milton rolled to his left, motioned to Smith to keep going, and then fired the ball across the field and all the way into the end zone for a 50-yard touchdown. NextGen stats measured Milton's throw at 64.4 air yards. The two hooked up again for a 45-yarder with 15 seconds left in the third quarter. That pulled the Eagles to within 31-17. They were down by just seven points when Ty Robinson blocked Bryan Anger's punt as Kenny Moore scooped it up and ran it back three yards for a touchdown. The Eagles were within a touchdown for the first time since they fell behind 7-0 on the Cowboys' opening drive. But the Cowboys came right back on Prescott's 19-yard run. Milton answered with a 15-yard TD of his own to make it 38-30 with 9:09 left after the Eagles went for the two-point conversion and failed. But the Eagles got a break when Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal with 3:23 left. The Eagles went right to work as Milton hit Makai Lemon from 24 yards out. Again, the two-point conversion failed. But the Eagles had one more chance after they stopped the Cowboys on fourth down on Ty Robinson's sack with 50 seconds left. Then the Eagles barely got close enough for Elliott's 60-yard field goal, the second longest of his career. Here are three more takeaways: Joe Milton has a memorable game It was just Milton's third career start. But the Eagles' quarterback, a member of the Cowboys practice squad before the Eagles signed him on Oct. 16, made things happen with his arm (two long TDs) and his legs (a 15-yard TD run). In all, Milton was 21 of 31 for 331 yards and 3 touchdowns. Was it a fumble that could've turned game around? It appeared that Cowboys running back Javonte Williams fumbled the ball at the goal line late in the first half. On 1st-and-goal from the 1, Williams was stopped by Eagles defensive tackle Ty Robinson and the ball came out. Riq Woolen recovered the ball and was running towards the Cowboys end zone. But the play was blown dead as the officials said Williams' forward progress was stopped. Had it been ruled a fumble, and an Eagles touchdown, the Eagles would have cut the Cowboys' lead to 21-17. Instead, the Cowboys kept possession and scored with 4 seconds left in the half for a 28-10 lead. Rough game for Quinyon Mitchell Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell had his hands full against Cowboys receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. And that was before Cooper DeJean left early in the game with a concussion. Mitchell was called for three defensive penalties in the first half alone − two defensive pass interference calls and an illegal contact call. The second pass interference call was on Prescott's pass to CeeDee Lamb into the end zone, thus giving the Cowboys a first down at the Eagles' 1 yard line with less than a minute left in the first half. The Cowboys scored with 4 seconds left in the first half for a 28-10 lead. It wasn't just Mitchell, who was selected to the Pro Bowl in each of the last two seasons. Riq Woolen also had a tough time covering the Cowboys receivers. Woolen was beaten for a 36-yard completion to Pickens in the first quarter that set up the Cowboys' second touchdown. title: Terry Bradshaw calls Aaron Rodgers 'strange' and hopes he goes away
summary: Terry Bradshaw didn't hold back on Fox, calling Aaron Rodgers a "strange" guy and saying he hopes he keeps his promise to disappear.
content: Terry Bradshaw called the Pittsburgh Steelers a classy organization Thursday evening. The Steelers Hall of Famer had much harsher words for Aaron Rodgers. "Am I surprised? Absolutely not. In my opinion, he's a strange guy anyway," the NFL analyst said during Fox's Thanksgiving pregame show. Bradshaw, who won four Super Bowls as the Steelers' quarterback from 1970 to 1983, also brought up Rodgers' vow to disappear once he is done playing. "And I hope this is one time he is telling the truth," Bradshaw said. Rodgers gave Bradshaw plenty of reason for the spicy comments. A day earlier, after the Steelers benched him for Mason Rudolph, Rodgers went on "The Pat McAfee Show," accused coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping through team meetings and said he wasn't coming back. The Steelers waived him that afternoon. Bradshaw said he has been friends with McCarthy for years and didn't know all the details, but he knew enough. "None of us turn on our teammates," Bradshaw said to the panel of former players with whom he co-hosts. "We don't turn on our coaching. We don't turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out. "Aaron Rodgers didn't do that." Bradshaw had never wanted Rodgers in Pittsburgh. In May 2025, while the Steelers were courting Rodgers, Bradshaw told 103.7 The Buzz in Arkansas that the quarterback should stay in California and "chew on bark." Rodgers, 43, laughed it off at the time. Now, the Steelers continue their season with Rudolph at quarterback , starting with the Black Friday game against the Broncos . Rodgers' future is up in the air. He's already said on McAfee's show that he's not going to be calling teams searching for new opportunities. "When this is done, it's Keyser Soze," Rodgers said. "And you won't see me." This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Terry Bradshaw calls Aaron Rodgers 'strange' and hopes he goes away

title: ‘Tom Brady Is Disgusted With Aaron Rodgers’ — NFL World Reacts As Legendary QB Makes Feelings Clear on Steelers-Mike McCarthy Controversy
summary: During Thursday’s Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys broadcast on FOX, Tom Brady addressed the messy split between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. He kept his tone calm and measured, but his message landed hard with many viewers.
content: ‘Tom Brady Is Disgusted With Aaron Rodgers’ — NFL World Reacts As Legendary QB Makes Feelings Clear on Steelers-Mike McCarthy Controversy During Thursday’s Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys broadcast on FOX, Tom Brady addressed the messy split between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. He kept his tone calm and measured, but his message landed hard with many viewers. The NFL legend and FOX analyst built his comments around what he called the sanctity of the locker room, and he said private matters should not be made public. Many fans and analysts heard that as a pointed rebuke of Rodgers. Reactions online came quickly, and several people said Brady had all but called Rodgers a bad teammate. Tom Brady Defends Sacred NFL Locker Room After Steelers Cut Aaron Rodgers The Steelers cut Rodgers, their starting quarterback and a four-time NFL MVP, after he went on Pat McAfee’s show on Wednesday and “basically burned the house down,” as Brady put it, criticizing Mike McCarthy and the whole organization. “It was a weird situation,” Brady said. He noted that the Steelers have a game on Friday and said they all now have to deal with the aftermath. For Brady, that was the core of the problem. The damage, in his view, does not stay with one player. It spills onto everyone else in the room. Brady then made the point he clearly wanted viewers to hear. He said an NFL locker room is “a very sacred place,” adding that “we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players.” “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room, you’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together,” he said, adding that the locker room should not be the place for “private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” BUILD YOUR TEAM’S DRAFT: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Brady did not dismiss what Rodgers has done on the field. He called Rodgers a Hall of Famer and said he is “a tremendous player.” He also said his criticism had “nothing to do with his play style.” Then came one of the more striking lines of the segment. “If that’s the last pass he throws, that’s a really sad way to end,” Brady said. From there, Brady drew on his own career. He said he was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years. “What made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and your coaches and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish,” he said. A moment later, he added: “And that supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you wanna promote.” PICK THE PLAYOFF FIELD: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Brady said again that he was fortunate to be in a great locker room. “I played for my teammates, I played for my coaches,” he said. He then closed with a line that summed up his view of the whole situation: “nobody wins when the family feuds.” Fans and Analysts React to Brady Burying Rodgers With Polite Criticism Brady never directly called Rodgers selfish or a bad teammate. Still, people read between the lines. Robin Lundberg, a WNBA analyst, put it bluntly in a post on X: “Tom Brady is disgusted with Aaron Rodgers.” Many fans read the comments the same way. They saw Brady choosing his words carefully while still making his feelings plain. One fan wrote that Brady “is doing everything he can right now to not call Rodgers a selfish loser. Basically said it as politely as possible.” Sports announcer Chase Snyder made a similar point about how far Brady went without saying the words outright, noting that “Tom Brady just said Aaron Rodgers is a bad teammate in every way he possibly could without directly saying he’s a bad teammate.” Jarrett Bailey, an NFL analyst, focused on the contrast between Brady’s tone and the weight of what he said. “Tom Brady just very politely and professionally buried Aaron Rodgers,” Bailey wrote. Not everyone thought Brady went quite that far. One fan called it “a light scolding for Aaron Rodgers from Tom Brady there.” Some fans also praised the way Brady handled such a touchy subject on live TV. “Brady, in a very professional way took care of the Rodgers situation. Well done,” one fan wrote. Taken together, the reaction showed how sharply Brady’s words cut, even in a mild tone. He praised Rodgers as a player and called a possible end to his career sad. But he also made clear that, in his view, airing a team’s private business in public crosses a line. As Brady pointed out, the Steelers now have to play on Friday while dealing with the fallout, and for many viewers his core message was easy to hear. title: Why even Trent Williams envies the high point of new 49ers starter Vederian Lowe's career
summary: Vederian Lowe has big shoes to fill with Colton McKivitz out. But the San Francisco 49ers' newest starter has one feat to his credit that even future Hall of Famer Trent Williams wishes he'd done.
content: San Francisco 49ers offensive tackle Vederian Lowe (76) blocks during an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals in Santa Clara, Calif., Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Scot Tucker) (Scot Tucker/AP) Vederian Lowe has picked Trent Williams ' brain and studied the generational left tackle's film since signing with the San Francisco 49ers in March, but the onetime sixth-round pick and part-time NFL starter understands there are limits to what he can replicate. "A lot of the things that he does, I can't do," Lowe said. "Because Trent is one of one." However, there is something Lowe has done that Williams has spent his illustrious 16-season career wishing he could do. On Nov. 17, 2024, Lowe, then with the Patriots, realized every 300-pound man's dream when he caught a 4-yard touchdown from quarterback Drake Maye in a loss to the Chargers. Asked where his lone catch ranks among his career highlights, Lowe smiled and invoked Williams, who is catch-less and has long lobbied head coach Kyle Shanahan for a goal-line pass. "That (catch) might be number one because they don't come by - I was talking to Trent and even Trent doesn't have one," Lowe said. "So I'm like, ‘OK.' That's up there for sure." The lofty ranking Lowe has assigned his reception speaks to the rarity of such a snag. But it also speaks to the modest number of highlights he's collected in a five-season career that has included 25 starts, just four since Jan. 5, 2025. But that could be changing. Last Sunday, in a 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City, Lowe was unexpectedly thrust into the role of a key starter on a Super Bowl contender when right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a broken and dislocated ankle in the second quarter . McKivitz's season is over. Lowe's chance to show why the 49ers signed him to a two-year contract with a maximum value of $12 million to serve as their swing tackle is just beginning. "That's why we brought him here," Shanahan said. "Anytime you have a swing tackle - that means you better be capable of starting. He's started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter. And that's why we targeted him." Lowe is assuming some sizable cleats. McKivitz, 30, was earning every bit of the three-year, $45 million extension he signed last year by not allowing a sack in 327 pass-blocking snaps this season before his injury. The very early returns, however, are promising. On Lowe's first snap after replacing McKivitz, he pancaked defensive tackle Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins on a 10-yard run by Christian McCaffrey . It was the start of a 38-snap performance in which Lowe committed a false start, but he didn't allow a QB pressure on 19 pass-blocking snaps against Minnesota's chaotic, blitz-heavy defense, a unit which leads the NFL in sacks. Lowe did so despite logging most of his snaps at left tackle throughout his career. His only four starts at right tackle were in 2023 with the Patriots and he'd spent most of his practice time on the left side since joining the 49ers. "Swinging from both sides," Lowe said, "it's not an easy task at all." Center Jake Brendel wasn't surprised Lowe managed to make it look seamless. Brendel, 34, was struck by the questions Lowe was asking about the 49ers' intricate blocking schemes not long after his arrival. Lowe peppered Brendel with queries about "chokes," "blunts" and "seals," all backside blocks from tight ends or other players lined up outside the 49ers' offensive tackles. "He asked me questions that guys don't ask me until year three or four in the system," Brendel said. "So the guy knows football … A lot of backup tackles kind of just float around and then they go in and they're like, ‘All right, I'll get it done physically, but I'm not expecting to be at the level of a starter.' This guy's definitely starting (material)." The Patriots weren't convinced about Lowe's first-string ability. After Lowe made a season-high 13 starts in 2024, New England drafted left tackle Will Campbell with the No. 4 pick to replace him last year. Lowe made four starts as a fill-in in 2025 after making 21 starts the previous two seasons. After his step down in status, he joined the 49ers knowing he'd have no shot to unseat Williams or McKivitz. Now, however, he's a starter on a 9-1 team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. Lowe has a chance to help his new team earn a ring while showing he's more than a well-compensated backup. If last Sunday's performance was any indication, it's an opportunity he's ready to seize, much like that pass he caught in 2024, a moment even Williams can only hope to replicate. "The opportunity doesn't come by too often," Lowe said, "and I was not dropping that." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. title: Wu-Tang Clan takes over Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving halftime show
summary: The legendary rap collective tore through decades of classics during the Lions-Bears game, with Eminem curating the performance and Chad
content: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: The Wu-Tang Clan performs the halftime show during the game between the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Photo by: Gregory Shamus / Getty Images The legendary rap collective tore through decades of classics during the Lions-Bears game, with Eminem curating the performance and Chad Smith joining on drums. Thanksgiving came with a side of Shaolin at Ford Field. Wu-Tang Clan took over the Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving Day halftime show on Thursday, delivering a rapid-fire run through the songs that helped establish the Staten Island collective as one of hip-hop’s most influential groups. The group hit the field during the Lions’ matchup against the Chicago Bears dressed in Detroit blue and backed by Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith. The group opened with “Triumph” before moving through a medley that reportedly included “Da Mystery of Chessboxin’,” “Protect Ya Neck,” “Method Man,” “Shimmy Shimmy Ya,” “Ice Cream,” “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” Young Dirty Bastard stepped in to represent his late father, founding Wu-Tang member Ol’ Dirty Bastard, during “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.” Before the show, he shared a backstage photo with Eminem, who helped bring the performance together. Eminem did not join Wu-Tang onstage, but his fingerprints were all over the production. According to Complex , the Detroit rapper and his longtime manager, Paul Rosenberg, served as executive producers and selected the group to headline the show. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Detroit Lions (@detroitlionsnfl) The performance marked the second year of their multiyear partnership with the Lions. In 2025, Eminem made a surprise appearance alongside Jack White during the team’s Thanksgiving game, performing “‘Till I Collapse” before the Detroit rock star closed the set with “Seven Nation Army.” When Wu-Tang’s appearance was announced earlier this month, Lions President and CEO Rich Haddad described the holiday game as one of sports’ greatest traditions and the group as one of music’s greatest acts. “We are thrilled to have Wu-Tang headlining our Thanksgiving halftime show and grateful to Marshall and Paul for their partnership,” Haddad said in the NFL’s announcement . The booking arrived during an already celebratory period for the group. Less than two weeks before the Thanksgiving performance, Wu-Tang Clan received the Early Influence Award at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony. Chris Rock inducted the group, praising its members for building a global hip-hop force without relying on the traditional industry machine. Wu-Tang then performed another crowd-pleasing medley featuring “C.R.E.A.M.,” “Method Man” and “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.” The latest honor follows the group’s “Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber” tour, which was announced as its final North American run. RZA previously described the tour as a chance for the members to come together once more and spread Wu-Tang’s music and culture around the world. Thursday’s halftime show proved that whether the stage is an arena, an awards ceremony or the middle of a football field, the Clan still knows how to command a crowd. title: Andrey Rublev shares his honest opinion about Mirra Andreeva as both a tennis player and person

content: Andrey Rublev experienced playing alongside Mirra Andreeva at the US Open this year. Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals this year, in what has been a big breakthrough season for the Russian teenager, who has a big opportunity to become world number one at the start of the 2027 season. Although they had played an exhibition set together before, the US Open mixed doubles was the first time Andreeva and Rublev had played together in a professional setting. Andreeva and Rublev made it all the way to the semi-finals, beating two-time defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori en route, before they were beaten by eventual champions Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik . Three months on from playing with Andreeva, Rublev has revealed what he really thinks about his compatriot. Andrey Rublev backs Mirra Andreeva to achieve a lot more in her career While Andreeva has mostly had success this year, it has been a mixed season for former world number five Rublev, who dropped outside the top 20 for the first time in six years this season. Following the conclusion of his 2026 season, Rublev appeared on the The Blueprint , where he was asked about Andreeva and his experience of playing with her at the US Open this year. Rublev was full of praise for Andreeva, who he predicted would go on to achieve a lot more success in her career. “She’s such a good, joyful, bright, sunny child, incredibly talented, who has already achieved a lot and will achieve even more,” said Rublev. “I knew right away it would be a great atmosphere [US Open mixed doubles], so yeah, I think we had a blast. We also managed to show a good level of play, considering neither Mirra nor I are doubles players. It left behind some great memories that I’ll definitely cherish.” Andreeva has played with both Rublev and Daniil Medvedev , the latter of whom she lost in the first round with, in US Open mixed doubles since the event was overhauled in 2025. It will be interesting to see if Andreeva partakes in the event again in 2027 and if she reunites with either Rublev or Medvedev, or if she has a new partner.
